## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning (15/5)

## Definitions

- [statement] Contention is not a general protection against leakage abuse: the 2023 ETH analysis of preview-era equality QE found that query logs could reunite values across contention tokens. That result is historical evidence, not a demonstrated attack on current range-index tuning. (low confidence) — https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/infk/inst-infsec/appliedcrypto/research/Security-Analysis-of-MongoDB-Queryable-Encryption.pdf · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Set realistic inclusive min/max bounds to improve range efficiency; use the field's BSON type. Bounds are required when precision is specified. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-encryption/client-side-encryption.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] SERVER-92390 documents a historical small-domain failure: an unspecified trimFactor with a domain of six or fewer bits could produce 'Trim factor must be less than the number of bits used to represent the domain.' The tracker lists fixes in 8.0.0-rc14 and 8.1.0-rc0; this is not evidence of a current unfixed defect. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-92390 · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Contention partitions per-value counters into randomly selected slots; increasing it reduces collisions for concurrent same-value writes but increases read work. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/infk/inst-infsec/appliedcrypto/research/Security-Analysis-of-MongoDB-Queryable-Encryption.pdf
- [statement] Queryable Encryption partitions each field/value counter into contention + 1 slots and randomly selects a slot on insertion, reducing conflicts between concurrent writes of repeated values. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/infk/inst-infsec/appliedcrypto/research/Security-Analysis-of-MongoDB-Queryable-Encryption.pdf
- [statement] trimFactor removes root levels from the encrypted range tree. Raising it reduces write conflicts and improves insert throughput, while slowing broad range reads. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/crypto/encryption_fields.idl
- [statement] Lower sparsity produces faster range queries with greater metadata storage overhead. MongoDB documents default 2 and a maximum increase from 4 to 8 in version 8.2; current repository validation permits 1–8. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/crypto/encryption_fields.idl
- [statement] For double/decimal fields, precision truncates query digits without rounding or altering the stored encrypted value; reducing precision limits index overhead. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning
- [statement] The consulted manual specifies defaults contention=8, sparsity=2 and trimFactor=6; SERVER-91077 records the latter two defaults. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-91077
- [statement] Explicit-encryption RangeOpts must match the destination encryptedFields configuration for min, max, trimFactor, sparsity and precision; double/decimal128 min/max/precision must be supplied together or all omitted. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-encryption/client-side-encryption.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning
- [statement] Spring Data MongoDB 5.0 documents range configuration through @RangeEncrypted with contentionFactor and rangeOptions, including bounds and floating-point precision examples. (low confidence) — https://www.springframework.org/spring-data/mongodb/reference/5.0/mongodb/mongo-encryption.html · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning
- [statement] Spring Data MongoDB exposes range configuration through @RangeEncrypted and collection options. Its examples combine contentionFactor=8 with integer bounds 0–150, and use typed BSON bounds for decimal-valued fields. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.springframework.org/spring-data/mongodb/reference/5.0/mongodb/mongo-encryption.html · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-encryption/client-side-encryption.md
- [statement] Omit a query type for encrypted fields that never need encrypted searches to avoid generating their searchable indexes. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/what-is-the-performance-comparison-between-queryable-encryption-and-csfle-if-im-looking-to-encrypt-strings-of-size-in-kbs-stored-in-mongo-db-cluster/290618
- [statement] The documented automatic-encryption contention default is 8; the server configuration also declares 8. Explicit encryption requires a contention value. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/crypto/encryption_fields.idl
- [statement] Treat database snapshots accompanied by query transcripts/logs as outside current QE security guarantees, especially for range queries. The historical ETH study illustrates why logs require a separate threat-model review; increasing tuning parameters does not establish protection against this adversary. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md · keywords: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning · also: https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/infk/inst-infsec/appliedcrypto/research/Security-Analysis-of-MongoDB-Queryable-Encryption.pdf
